decisions.statement: A body is read to text once.
The text read is kept for a caller to look at.
A body that cannot be read reads as an empty body.
Nothing here tells an unreadable body from an empty body.
The error type is parsed from the text read.
Nothing a body can hold makes the error type parse throw.
A response to hand on is built only when a caller asks for a response.
Each ask builds a response of its own.
A rebuilt response has the status of the original.
A rebuilt response has the status text of the original.
A rebuilt response has the headers of the original.
A rebuilt response has a headers object of its own.
No decision here is made from the status.
A rebuilt response has the content-encoding of a body already decoded.
A rebuilt response has the content-length of the compressed body.

definition: a response read to text with a replacement response left in place
